items.title: RSS Wants to Reach Gen Z. It’s Been Doing This for Decades | LME 154 | Pooja Prasanna
items.summary: The RSS’s Sarsanghachalak or its chief Mohan Bhagwat just met more than 2,000 Gen Z and Gen Alpha students from across India. The timing was deliberate- coming right on the heels of the protests over the NEET paper leak that forced Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation. Bhagwat played the sympathetic elder- backing the youth, calling protest a legitimate part of democracy, and asserting that questioning power isn’t anti-national. All this while not overtly criticising the government. Many saw it as the RSS reaching out to a new generation. But there's nothing new about it. The RSS has always been about catching them young. That India’s future must be shaped from its classrooms. In fact, one of their first major initiatives after Independence wasn't political at all. It was educational: opening a primary school in Uttar Pradesh in 1952, as noted by historian Tanika Sarkar. That’s why schools, colleges, textbooks, teachers, and universities have remained central to the Sangh Parivar’s long-term project. Today, that influence extends far beyond the RSS’s own schools. items.title: Bengaluru cops detain hundreds of people in ‘illegal migrant’ drive, activists accuse assault
items.summary: Hours after Bengaluru Police launched a citywide drive to identify suspected illegal immigrants, a group of civil liberties organisations has accused the force of illegally detaining and assaulting hundreds of migrant workers, including women and children. In a complaint to the Karnataka Home Minister, the Peoples Union for Civil Liberties (PUCL), All India Lawyers Association for Justice (AILAJ), Domestic Workers Rights Union (DWRU), and All India Central Council of Trade Unions (AICCTU) alleged that police teams entered slum settlements across the city early Saturday, August 8, detaining people in the name of identifying Bangladeshi nationals. They said the people detained were predominantly poor, daily-wage and migrant workers. According to the complaint, police entered homes between 6:30 and 7:30 am and, even after residents produced identity documents, forced some into police vehicles and took them to police stations, convention centres and marriage halls. Lawyers and activists from the four organisations visited these sites and spoke with detainees and officials. items.title: Driver and conductor killed as Kozhikode-Bengaluru KSRTC bus overturns near Bidadi
items.summary: Two people were killed and 25 others injured after a Kerala State Road Transport Corporation (KSRTC) bus travelling to Bengaluru overturned after crashing into a directional signboard on the Bengaluru-Mysuru Highway near Avaragere Gate in Bengaluru South district on Saturday, August 8. The deceased have been identified as Mithan and Arun Kumar, the conductor and driver of the bus, respectively. Both were from Kerala and were in their 40s. A senior police officer from Bidadi said one of the 25 injured passengers is in critical condition after suffering severe head injuries. The accident occurred around 6.30 am when the bus veered to the left and rammed into a directional signboard before overturning. A passenger alerted the police, following which personnel from the Bidadi police and fire department launched a rescue operation. The injured were taken to nearby hospitals for treatment. Several passengers suffered injuries to their hands, legs and upper body, though most were reported to be out of danger. items.title: Telangana School Education Dept says private schools must make fee details public
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. The Telangana School Education Department has instructed private unaided schools to make their fee structures for the 2026–27 academic year publicly available to parents and students. Under the latest directions, schools must display class-wise fee details at their campuses and publish the same information on their official websites. The fee details must also be uploaded to the Telangana School Education Department’s official portal, schooledu.telangana.gov.in. Telangana state director of school education E Naveen Nicolas said Regional Joint Directors and District Educational Officers have been asked to ensure that private unaided schools comply with the directions. The department has created a dedicated facility on its portal through which school managements can submit their fee details. Schools are also required to upload the documents used to arrive at the fee amounts for each class. These supporting records must be signed by members of the school’s governing body and prepared in accordance with the provisions of the relevant 1994 Government Order.
